definitions.gloss: outside rounds; visiting clients; outside sales
definitions.explanation: Going outside the office to visit clients, make deliveries, or conduct business at external locations. A common part of many sales and service jobs in Japan.
The outer circle of a loop line (such as the Yamanote Line in Tokyo) or the outer circumference of something.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{外回|そとまわ}りの{日|ひ}だ。
examples.english: Today is a day for outside visits.

examples.japanese: {営業|えいぎょう}の{外回|そとまわ}りで{一日中|いちにちじゅう}{歩|ある}き{回|まわ}った。
examples.english: I walked around all day doing outside sales calls.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}の{日|ひ}の{外回|そとまわ}りは{大変|たいへん}だが、{客先|きゃくさき}には{時間|じかん}どおりに{着|つ}かなければならない。
examples.english: Doing outside rounds on a rainy day is tough, but you have to arrive at the client's on time.

examples.japanese: {山手線|やまのてせん}の{外回|そとまわ}りに{乗|の}る。
examples.english: To ride the outer loop of the Yamanote Line.

examples.japanese: {外回|そとまわ}りと{内回|うちまわ}りを{間違|まちが}えて{反対方向|はんたいほうこう}に{乗|の}ってしまった。
examples.english: I mixed up the outer and inner loops and got on in the wrong direction.

examples.japanese: {外回|そとまわ}りホームは{階段|かいだん}を{上|あ}がって{右側|みぎがわ}です。
examples.english: The outer loop platform is on the right after going up the stairs.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1 is a common business term. Office workers who spend time visiting clients are said to be doing {外回|そとまわ}り, in contrast to {内勤|ないきん} (office/desk work).

Sense 2 is used for circular train lines and tracks. On the Yamanote Line, {外回|そとまわ}り goes clockwise and {内回|うちまわ}り goes counterclockwise.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {外回|そとまわ}りの{営業|えいぎょう} (outside sales)
- {外回|そとまわ}りに{出|で}る (to go out on rounds)
- {山手線|やまのてせん}{外回|そとまわ}り (Yamanote Line outer loop)
